cards.text: Our story opens in Canaan, where Jacob, the father of twelve sons (Genesis 35:22), is living in the same land his father lived in. Jacob's son Joseph is seventeen, out tending the flock with some of his brothers, the sons of his father's wives Bilhah and Zilpah. And when Joseph checks in with Dad, friend, he has NEWS.

cards.question: What kind of report does seventeen-year-old Joseph bring his father about those brothers?

cards.text: Jacob also goes by Israel (Genesis 32:28), and Israel loves Joseph more than his other sons. So he makes Joseph a robe of many colors.

cards.question: Why does Israel love Joseph more than his other sons?

answers.text: Joseph was born in his old age

cards.text: The brothers see it plain as day: Dad loves Joseph more than any of them. And now the kid walks around in a robe of many colors, which is basically a billboard that says FAVORITE.

cards.question: Joseph's brothers see that their father loves Joseph more than any of them. How do they feel about Joseph?
Joseph's brothers can't speak a kind word to him.

cards.text: Then Joseph has a dream, and he tells it to his brothers. The brothers who can't say ONE kind word to him? THOSE brothers? Friend. Read the room.
In the dream, they're all binding sheaves of grain in a field. Suddenly Joseph's sheaf rises and stands upright.

cards.question: In Joseph's dream, his sheaf of grain stands upright. What do his brothers' sheaves do?

answers.text: They fall flat on the ground
They blow away in the wind

cards.question: Joseph's brothers answer his sheaf dream with a question: “Do you intend to reign over us?”

cards.text: So the brothers hate him even more, and then Joseph has ANOTHER dream and tells them AGAIN. Friend, the brakes on this young man's mouth are just for decoration.

cards.question: In Joseph's second dream, the sun and moon and eleven ___ bow down to him.

cards.text: Berry, my little star, would've LOVED that dream, but this time Joseph tells his father too. And Israel rebukes him: “Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”

cards.question: Joseph's brothers are jealous of him, and Israel, after rebuking Joseph, puts the whole dream out of his mind.

cards.text: Some time later, the brothers take their father's flocks to pasture near Shechem. Israel tells Joseph, “Get ready; I am sending you to them.”
“I am ready,” Joseph replies. No hesitation, friend, and that's exactly the energy I want when I call a baker to the ovens.

cards.question: Israel is sending Joseph to his brothers at Shechem. What is Joseph's job?

answers.text: See how they and the flocks are faring
Bring his brothers home to Hebron
Count the sheep in every flock

cards.text: Joseph heads out from the Valley of Hebron, gets to Shechem, and a man finds him wandering in the field asking where his brothers are. I picture him like the guy who drives across town to the old office after the company already moved.

cards.question: The man in the field heard Joseph's brothers say where they were going next. Where did they go?

cards.text: The brothers spot Joseph coming from a distance and say to one another, “Here comes that dreamer!” Before he even reaches them, they plot to kill him.

cards.question: The brothers plan to kill Joseph and throw him into a pit. What do they plan to say happened to him?

answers.text: Robbers attacked him on the road
He got lost in the wilderness

cards.text: And they add, “Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!” But Reuben, Jacob's firstborn (Genesis 35:23), hears this and tells them not to take Joseph's life.

cards.question: Reuben tells his brothers, “Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him.” Why does Reuben say this?

answers.text: So he can rescue Joseph and return him home
So Joseph will learn his lesson down there
So nobody will ever blame the brothers

cards.text: Joseph walks up, and the brothers strip him of his robe. THE robe. The robe of many colors he's wearing.

cards.question: The pit the brothers throw Joseph into is full of water.

cards.text: Then the brothers sit down to eat a meal, with Joseph down in that pit. They look up and see a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, camels carrying spices, balm and myrrh.

cards.question: The Ishmaelite caravan is on its way down to ___.

cards.text: Then Judah, another of Jacob's sons (Genesis 35:23), speaks up: “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?”

cards.question: Judah has a new plan for the caravan: “Come, let us ___ him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.”

cards.text: The brothers agree. So when the Midianite traders pass by, they pull Joseph out of the pit and sell him to the Ishmaelites, who take him to Egypt.

cards.question: How much do the brothers sell Joseph for?

cards.text: Back at the pit, Reuben returns. He looks in, and Joseph is not there.

cards.question: Reuben finds the pit empty. What does he do?

answers.text: He goes to tell his father

cards.text: Reuben goes back to his brothers: “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?” Then they take Joseph's robe and slaughter a young goat.

cards.question: The brothers have Joseph's robe and a slaughtered young goat. What do they do with the robe?

answers.text: Dip it in the goat's blood

cards.text: They send the robe of many colors to their father with a message: “We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe or not.”

cards.question: Jacob recognizes the robe and says a vicious animal has devoured Joseph.
Jacob tears his clothes and puts sackcloth around his waist. How long does he mourn for his son?
All of Jacob's sons and daughters try to comfort him, and he lets them.

cards.text: “No,” he says. “I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.” And his father weeps for him.

cards.question: Meanwhile, the Midianites sell Joseph in ___ to Potiphar, the captain of the guard.

cards.text: That buyer, Potiphar, is an officer of Pharaoh, Egypt's king. And that's where we leave Joseph for now, friend, a long way from home, and trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "Come, let us ___ him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1 by a wide margin: 6 multiple choice cards (2, 4, 6, 10, 18, 20), 3 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "Friend. Read the room." makes Joseph the butt of the joke by scolding him for telling his dream. The text gives no judgment on whether he should have told it.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They fall flat on the ground" is close to bowing down, which the passage itself calls bowing "down to the ground" (Genesis 37:10). A baker could argue it is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "The brakes on this young man's mouth are just for decoration" laughs at Joseph and calls him careless. It does not laugh with his situation, and the text makes no such judgment.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: The Berry line does not click. It is unclear why a star-shaped cutter would love a dream where stars bow down, and the "but" that joins it to Joseph telling his father doesn't connect the two ideas. The card also packs in the Berry aside, Joseph telling his father and Israel's rebuke.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: "That's exactly the energy I want when I call a baker to the ovens" is pleasant but not funny. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card has more than two things happening: Joseph leaves Hebron and arrives at Shechem, a man finds him wandering and they talk about his brothers, and then there is an office-move joke.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke about driving to the old office after the company moved tells that the brothers have moved on. That comes from Genesis 37:17 ("They have moved on from here"), but the card cites only Genesis 37:14-16.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The stop 2 story cards (1, 3, 7, 9, 11) are plain retelling with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Only card 5 ("THE robe.") has any. This stop holds the most dramatic turns in the passage: the plot to kill Joseph, the meal beside the pit and the sale.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The stop 3 story cards (1, 3, 5, 9) are bare retelling with no storyteller lines or reactions from Papa Dorin. The grief here calls for a tender voice rather than jokes, but his voice is missing altogether until the closing card.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
